questions.prompt: A displacement is given by \(3\mathbf i+4\mathbf j\) m. Find its magnitude and state its direction as an angle above the positive \(x\)-axis.
questions.answer: The magnitude is \(\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5\) m. The direction angle satisfies \(\tan\theta=4/3\), so \(\theta=\tan^{-1}(4/3)\approx 53.1^\circ\).

questions.prompt: A car travels with velocity \(12\) m s\(^{-1}\) due east. Identify the magnitude, direction, and units of the vector.
questions.answer: The magnitude is \(12\), the direction is due east, and the units are m s\(^{-1}\). All three pieces describe the velocity vector.

questions.prompt: For \(\mathbf a=(-5,12)\), calculate \(|\mathbf a|\).
questions.answer: Use the magnitude formula: \(|\mathbf a|=\sqrt{(-5)^2+12^2}=\sqrt{169}=13\).

questions.prompt: A vector has magnitude \(10\) and direction \(30^\circ\) above the positive \(x\)-axis. Find its Cartesian components.
questions.answer: The components are \((10\cos30^\circ,10\sin30^\circ)=(5\sqrt3,5)\).

questions.prompt: Classify mass \(4\) kg, force \(7\) N north, temperature \(18^\circ\)C, and acceleration \(3\) m s\(^{-2}\) downward as scalar or vector quantities.
questions.answer: Mass and temperature have no direction, so they are scalars. Force and acceleration include directions, so they are vectors.

questions.prompt: Point \(A=(2,-1)\) and point \(B=(8,7)\). Find \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) and its length.
questions.answer: Subtract coordinates: \(\overrightarrow{AB}=(8-2,7-(-1))=(6,8)\). Its length is \(\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\).

questions.prompt: A ship sails \(6\) km east and \(8\) km north. Write the displacement vector and find its distance from the start.
questions.answer: The displacement is \(6\mathbf i+8\mathbf j\) km. Its magnitude is \(\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\) km.

questions.prompt: For \(\mathbf v=(-2,6,3)\), find \(|\mathbf v|\) and a unit vector in the same direction.
questions.answer: The magnitude is \(\sqrt{4+36+9}=7\). The unit vector is \(\mathbf v/7=(-2/7,6/7,3/7)\).

questions.prompt: A displacement is \(20\) m at bearing \(060^\circ\). Using east as \(x\) and north as \(y\), find its components.
questions.answer: A bearing is measured from north, so east component is \(20\sin60^\circ=10\sqrt3\) and north component is \(20\cos60^\circ=10\). The vector is \((10\sqrt3,10)\) m.

questions.prompt: Given \(\overrightarrow{OA}=(1,4,-2)\) and \(\overrightarrow{OB}=(-3,5,6)\), find \(\overrightarrow{AB}\).
questions.answer: Use \(\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}\). Thus \(\overrightarrow{AB}=(-3,5,6)-(1,4,-2)=(-4,1,8)\).

questions.prompt: A force vector is \(6\mathbf i-8\mathbf j\) N. Find its magnitude and its angle below the positive \(x\)-axis.
questions.answer: The magnitude is \(\sqrt{6^2+(-8)^2}=10\) N. The angle satisfies \(\tan\theta=8/6\), so \(\theta\approx53.1^\circ\) below the positive \(x\)-axis.

questions.prompt: A vector has components \((a,6)\) and magnitude \(10\). Find \(a\).
Find the position vector of the midpoint of \(A=(2,5,1)\) and \(B=(8,-1,7)\).
questions.answer: Average corresponding coordinates: \(((2+8)/2,(5-1)/2,(1+7)/2)=(5,2,4)\).

questions.prompt: A vector of magnitude \(13\) has positive \(x\)-component \(5\) and negative \(y\)-component. Find the vector.
questions.answer: Let the vector be \((5,y)\). Then \(25+y^2=169\), so \(y^2=144\). Since \(y\) is negative, the vector is \((5,-12)\).

questions.prompt: A plane has velocity \(80\) m s\(^{-1}\) north-east. Find its east and north components.
questions.answer: North-east means \(45^\circ\) to both axes, so each component is \(80\cos45^\circ=40\sqrt2\).

questions.prompt: For \(\mathbf u=(2,-1,2)\), find a vector of length \(15\) in the same direction.
questions.answer: Here \(|\mathbf u|=\sqrt{4+1+4}=3\). Scale by \(15/3=5\), giving \(5\mathbf u=(10,-5,10)\).

questions.prompt: A particle moves from \(P=(-1,3)\) to \(Q=(5,-5)\). Find the displacement vector, magnitude, and direction angle.
questions.answer: The displacement is \(Q-P=(6,-8)\). Its magnitude is \(10\). The angle is \(\tan^{-1}(-8/6)\approx -53.1^\circ\), measured from the positive \(x\)-axis.

questions.prompt: A vector \(\mathbf a=(3,4)\) is rotated to \(\mathbf b=(-4,3)\). Verify the rotation by comparing magnitudes and using a dot product to find the angle between them.
questions.answer: The magnitudes are \(|\mathbf a|=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5\) and \(|\mathbf b|=\sqrt{(-4)^2+3^2}=5\), so length is preserved. Their dot product is \(3(-4)+4(3)=0\). Since both vectors are non-zero, a zero dot product means the angle is \(90^\circ\). The change \((x,y)\mapsto(-y,x)\) is therefore a \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise rotation.

questions.prompt: The position of a drone relative to a controller is \((30,-40,20)\) m. Find its distance, unit line-of-sight vector, and the vector displacement needed to move it \(15\) m closer along the same line.
questions.answer: The distance is \(\sqrt{30^2+(-40)^2+20^2}=10\sqrt{29}\) m. The unit line-of-sight vector from the controller is \((3/\sqrt{29},-4/\sqrt{29},2/\sqrt{29})\). To move the drone \(15\) m closer to the controller, use the opposite direction with magnitude \(15\): \(-15(3/\sqrt{29},-4/\sqrt{29},2/\sqrt{29})=(-45/\sqrt{29},60/\sqrt{29},-30/\sqrt{29})\) m.

questions.prompt: A vector has magnitude \(15\), \(x\)-component \(9\), and positive \(y\)-component. Find the vector, its direction angle, and a unit vector perpendicular to it.
questions.answer: Use \(9^2+y^2=15^2\), so \(y^2=144\). Since \(y>0\), \(y=12\), giving \((9,12)\). The direction satisfies \(\tan\theta=12/9=4/3\), so \(\theta\approx53.1^\circ\). A perpendicular vector is \((-12,9)\), whose magnitude is \(15\), so a unit perpendicular vector is \((-4/5,3/5)\).
